facts.text: Cycle Toronto and two individuals announced Oct. 13 they are seeking leave to appeal to the Supreme Court over Ontario's bike lane removal law
Applicants Eva Stanger-Ross and Narada Kiondo join Cycle Toronto; counsel from Ecojustice and Paliare Roland Rosenberg Rothstein
Ontario Court of Appeal in August overturned the lower-court ruling that the removal plan violated Charter Section 7
The Supreme Court has not agreed to hear the appeal
Whether the leave application has been formally filed is not established
2024 provincial law lets Ontario remove about 19 km of protected bike lanes on Bloor, Yonge and University
Province says removal cuts congestion, which it says costs Ontario's economy $56 billion a year
Government-commissioned report found removals could raise collisions 54 per cent without meaningfully easing congestion
Removal of 1.2 km of Bloor West between Clissold Rd. and Royal York Rd. was slated to start the night of Oct. 13
Tuesday-night removal work was halted when protesters blocked pylon trucks, which were escorted off Bloor before 8 p.m.
The Supreme Court typically takes several months to decide on leave, too late to affect the Bloor removal
Toronto's mayoral election is about two weeks away, front-runners split on bike lanes
Bloor West bike lane removal in Etobicoke resumed Wednesday afternoon; crews removing markings, signs and concrete barriers
The work covers roughly one km of Bloor West from Clissold Rd. to Royal York Rd., starting west of Islington
Removal brings temporary vehicle lane reductions and is expected to finish in November
Two people were arrested during Wednesday's protest
Nina Thi Thi Tran, 25, of Hamilton charged with obstructing a peace officer and mischief under $5,000
A second person was arrested near Bloor West and Islington for mischief; charges not yet stated
Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria posted on X that work was 'halted by protesters' and the bike lanes 'are coming out'
Police Chief Myron Demkiw: no injunction prevents the removal; obstructing the lawful work can bring criminal charges
Mayor's spokesperson: work proceeded despite city proposals to keep bike lanes while restoring a traffic lane
City of Toronto media room lists no release or advisory on the bike lane removal through Oct. 13

missed.text: Court of Appeal said the trial judge misapplied the law and strayed into policy-making; lower court had 'effectively created a right to bike lanes where none existed'
The 2024 law also requires municipalities to seek provincial approval for new bike lanes that remove traffic lanes
Applicants want the Supreme Court to clarify whether Charter Section 7 applies to government decisions that increase risk to life and safety
Cycle Toronto executive director Michael Longfield said no network of side streets can replace the 19 km on Bloor, Yonge and University
Ecojustice lawyer Bronwyn Roe: 'The consequences of this case reach far beyond bike lanes'
Paliare Roland partner Andrew Lewis said applicants hope the court weighs whether 'common sense' can prevail over uncontested engineering evidence
Trial judge found the government pursued the plan despite its own advisers concluding it would not achieve its goal and could worsen congestion
Remaining sections of the removal are expected to begin next spring; province announced in September it would start on Bloor West
Mayor Olivia Chow's office says the city repeatedly shared designs keeping both vehicle and bike lanes; a stretch between Kipling and Islington kept its bike lane
Prior rides: about 850 cyclists on Danforth Aug. 30 and about 800 toward Royal York Sept. 30
In the past decade 28 people were killed and 380 seriously injured cycling in Toronto, per advocacy groups
Sarkaria's office did not answer questions on the location, duration or cost of the work
More than 30 police cruisers and a drone accompanied Wednesday's resumed work
No Ontario newsroom release on the Bloor removal this week; latest transportation release was Oct. 8 on Grimsby GO
